statement.title: A. Easy Problem
statement.legend: Cube is given an integer $n$. She wants to know how many ordered pairs of positive integers $(a,b)$ there are such that $a=n-b$. Since Cube is not very good at math, please help her!
statement.input_spec:
The first line contains an integer $t$ ($1 \leq t \leq 99$) — the number of test cases.

The only line of each test case contains an integer $n$ ($2 \leq n \leq 100$).
statement.output_spec: For each test case, output the number of ordered pairs $(a, b)$ on a new line.
statement.note:
In the first test case, the only ordered pair that works is $(a,b)=(1,1)$.

In the second test case, the three ordered pairs of $(a,b)$ that work are $(3,1), (2,2), (1,3)$.

Problem Credits: cry

Solution

For any $n$, Cube can set $a$ = any integer between $1$ and $n-1$ inclusive, and set $b = n - a$. $a$ cannot be less than $1$, because then it would be non-positive, and $a$ cannot be greater than $n-1$, because then $b$ would be less than $1$, which would make it non-positive. Therefore the answer is just $n-1$ for all $n$.
